changes.after: Let an object use a helper whose behavior can be swapped.

before: Composition means one object uses another object to perform part of its work. NoticeService has a Formatter; it is not a kind of Formatter. The constructor receives the collaborator explicitly.

Objects.requireNonNull checks the supplied reference and throws NullPointerException if absent. The final field prevents replacing that reference later, not every possible change inside the collaborator.
A second Formatter implementation can change formatting without subclassing NoticeService. This makes the dependency visible and allows small substitute implementations in tests.

Expected output or behavior: Ready
. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Create a test Formatter that returns a fixed value and confirm NoticeService delegates to it. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: Composition means one object uses another to do part of its work. NoticeService has a Formatter helper. Its constructor receives that helper, and message asks it to format the text.

Objects.requireNonNull returns the supplied reference or throws NullPointerException if it is missing. The final field keeps that same helper reference. It does not freeze any changeable data inside the helper.
Plain and Excited both provide the Formatter method. NoticeService can use either without changing its own code. A small replacement helper can also make the service easier to test.
The program prints Ready. Plain returns the supplied text unchanged, and NoticeService returns that result.
The quiz supplies Excited instead. The same message call now reaches a helper that adds an exclamation mark.

after.question: Supply new Excited() instead of new Plain(). What changes?

Both helpers run for every message.
after.explanation: NoticeService calls the Formatter it received. Excited adds the exclamation mark, so the result is Ready!.
